bullets: Game 4 of 8 in this single-deck session and the longest (285 s, decided in overtime at 0:13). Loss against a Sparky / Golden Knight / Mini P.E.K.K.A. / Evo Wizard / Giant-Vines beatdown list, after Ryley had taken the enemy right tower to 774 HP at clock 2:18.

The deck is piloted as bridge pressure, not as beatdown: Evolved Elite Barbarians go to a bridge five or six times (clock 2:35 [14, 14], clock 0:47 [3, 13], clock 0:21, overtime 1:48 [11, 3], overtime 1:09 [12, 7]) while the Rune Giant is held back and only appears in overtime as a tank in front of an existing push - "I don't really want to Rune Giant though" (clock 0:43).

The core package he recites is Evo E-Barbs + Minions + Heal Spirit with Zap in front: "Let's Zap Evo E-Barbs" (clock 0:21), "Do we need to go for the Heal Spirit as well so we don't lose our E-Barbs?" (clock 0:19), "Oh, man. E-Barbs, Minions, Heal Spirit" (overtime 1:09).

Stated win condition: "with the E-Barb being upgraded and the Rune Giant tanking, that is like a real three-crown threat" (clock 1:20) - the Rune Giant's enchant on fast-hitting Berserker and Elite Barbarians, kept alive by Heal Spirit and Savage Survival.

The two flexible slots are read-driven: Mother Witch is played because the opponent has no small spell ("cuz he has no Evo Zap", clock 0:29) and against enemy Minions (clock 1:34), and the Evo Zap is banked for the opponent's Vines (overtime 0:28) or cycled cheaply to get the Evolution back ("just to keep the HP in cycle to the Evo", overtime 1:04).

Weakness shown in this game: no answer to a big beatdown tank. Once the opponent stacked Giant + Vines behind an Evo Wizard, Ryley had only troops and a Fireball - "how are we going to stop getting three crown when he goes giant?" (overtime 1:50).

new_deck.display_name: Rune Giant Evo E-Barbs Hero Berserker
new_deck.rationale: At 3.25 average elixir the deck wins by dropping Evolved Elite Barbarians and the Hero Berserker directly at the bridge whenever the opponent commits elsewhere, with the 4-elixir Rune Giant used as a cheap forward tank for those fast hitters rather than as a back-line beatdown build-up.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The Rune Giant is the cheapest of the Giants and her enchant rewards fast attackers, which is exactly what the rest of the list is: Evolved Elite Barbarians, the Hero Berserker and Minions. Ryley states the plan himself - "with the E-Barb being upgraded and the Rune Giant tanking, that is like a real three-crown threat." Because the tank is only 4 elixir it can be played forward, at the bridge or in front of an already-committed push, so the deck applies pressure at bridge-spam speed instead of building from the back. Heal Spirit and the Berserker's Savage Survival ability keep those cheap threats alive through chip damage, while Mother Witch, Evolved Zap and Fireball cover swarms and support. Its weakness is the mirror of its strength: with no building and no heavy defensive tank, a real beatdown push (here Giant + Vines behind an Evolved Wizard) has to be answered with troops alone.
